author: Barry Revzin

evidence.note: P2287R0 proposed a single new syntax for naming base classes in designated initializers, using a colon designator (e.g., B{:A={.a=1}, .b=2}). It kept the rule that initializers must be all designated or none designated.
evidence.title: P2287R0 Designated-initializers for base classes
evidence.what_changed: R0 proposed a colon-based base-class designator. R1 dropped naming base classes entirely; R2 re-added indirect member initialization; R3 added direct initialization of base class subobjects without a designator; R6 retains the colon/base-naming approach as no longer considered.

evidence.note: In P2287R3 the author adopted both "directly initialize indirect members" (B{.a=1, .b=2}) and "allow mixing designated and non-designated initializers for base subobjects" (B{{.a=1}, .b=2}). He records that Varna EWG discussion showed desire for braces around base subobjects, that he allows optional braces but is 'strongly opposed to mandating braces,' arguing designated initialization should mirror assignment and that aggregate initialization already permits brace elision.
evidence.title: P2287R3 Designated-initializers for base classes
evidence.what_changed: R2 proposed only indirectly initializing members with designated syntax. R3 additionally allows directly initializing base class subobjects without a designator and allows optional (but not mandatory) braces around base subobjects; it also adds a clang implementation.

evidence.note: P2287R1 extended the R0 proposal to support both naming base classes with the colon designator and directly naming indirect non-static data members (B{.a=1, .b=2}), while keeping designated initializers order rules and all-designated-or-none rules.
evidence.title: P2287R1 Designated-initializers for base classes
evidence.what_changed: R0 named base classes only. R1 additionally allowed naming indirect non-static data members (the brace-elision form). Later revisions dropped the base-class naming designator entirely (R6 'eschews that approach').

evidence.note: P2287R2 dropped the base-class naming designator entirely and proposed only extending designated initializers to name direct or indirect non-static data members of aggregate base classes (B{.a=1, .b=2}), noting types like C:std::string or repeated member names could not be fully initialized and that naming base subobjects 'can be done later.'
evidence.title: P2287R2 Designated-initializers for base classes
evidence.what_changed: R1 supported both a colon base-class designator and indirect member naming; R2 removed base-class naming entirely to support only indirect member naming (the approach Matthias Stearn suggested). R3 then re-added the mixing rule for base subobjects with optional braces.

position: Barry Revzin has consistently documented support for extending C++ designated initializers to aggregates with base classes. Across P2287R0–R6 he first proposed a colon-based designator to name base classes, then dropped that in favor of initializing indirect non-static data members of aggregate bases (the Matthias Stearn suggestion), and by R3 he also endorsed allowing mixed designated/non-designated initializers where leading non-designated initializers initialize base subobjects. He records that after the Varna EWG discussion he accepted optional braces around base subobjects but is strongly opposed to mandating braces, arguing designated initialization should mirror assignment and that aggregate initialization already permits brace elision. He implements and updates the proposal (including a clang implementation) and has kept the core recommendation stable through R6.
recommendation: The paper proposes extending C++ designated initialization syntax to allow directly initializing base class aggregate elements, and to allow mixing designated and non-designated initializers when all non-designated initializers appear at the beginning of the initializer list and initialize base class subobjects.
title: Designated-initializers for Base Classes
